title: Northwest Airlines 705
summary: Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 705, a Boeing 720 operating from Miami to Portland via intermediate cities, crashed in the Florida Everglades on February 12, 1963, shortly after takeoff. The aircraft encountered a severe thunderstorm immediately after departure. While avoiding heavy turbulence, the aircraft encountered an extreme updraft that caused a pitch-up reaction, followed by pilot input that deepened the situation. The aircraft broke up in mid-air due to structural overstress from severe convective turbulence. All 43 aboard were killed in the crash.
probable_cause: Encounter with severe convective weather and extreme updraft during initial climb phase, structural failure from atmospheric overstress caused by severe thunderstorm turbulence exceeding aircraft design limits.

factors.evidence: Severe thunderstorm with extreme updraft encountered
Pilot control inputs during turbulent encounter
Aircraft broke up in mid-air from overstress
Loss of control during structural breakup

events.text: Flight 705 lifted off from Miami Runway 27L
Aircraft encountered severe updraft, nose-down then pitch-up reaction
Altitude increased rapidly at 9,000 feet per minute rate
Aircraft broke up in mid-air in severe thunderstorm

title: Trans-Canada Air Lines 831
summary: An in-flight fire developed and spread through the aircraft. Operating Air Canada, a Douglas DC-8, crashed killing all 118 people aboard. Poor weather and visibility conditions were identified as major contributing factors. The accident set records for aviation safety as one of the deadliest incidents of its time.

title: Pan Am 214
summary: Pan American World Airways Flight 214, a Boeing 707-121 named Clipper Tradewind, was operating from San Juan, Puerto Rico to Philadelphia with a scheduled stopover in Baltimore on December 8, 1963. After departure from Baltimore in the evening, the aircraft encountered a line of thunderstorms in the landing approach area. While in a holding pattern at 5,000 feet awaiting clearance to land, the aircraft experienced an explosion at 20:58 local time. The pilots transmitted a final mayday message indicating loss of control. The aircraft crashed in a corn field east of Elkton, Maryland, destroying itself in intense fires. All 81 passengers and crew aboard were killed. Civil Aeronautics Board investigation concluded that a lightning strike ignited fuel vapor in a fuel tank, causing the explosion that destroyed the left wing.
probable_cause: Lightning strike during thunderstorm operations ignited flammable fuel vapor in one of the aircraft's fuel tanks, causing a fuel tank explosion that destroyed the left wing and resulted in loss of aircraft control and crash.

factors.evidence: Thunderstorm with lightning activity at landing approach area
Lightning ignited flammable vapor in fuel tank
Aircraft lost control following structural damage
Intense post-crash fire destroyed aircraft and wreckage

Aircraft exploded, pilots transmitted final mayday before crash
Aircraft crashed in corn field east of Elkton Maryland, all 81 aboard killed
